request.spec:
A bulk settle is now all-or-nothing: if any selected claim cannot be settled by the signed-in
user (any refusal the single settle would give; going to PENDING is not a refusal), none of them is
settled, every one counts as refused and nothing is written. Otherwise every selected claim is
settled in list order as before, and after the claims' own lines one line BATCH_SETTLED
batch=<batch number> count=<claims in the batch> total=<the frozen figures of those SETTLED, added
up> is written.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A bulk settle is now all-or-nothing: if any selected claim cannot be settled by the signed-in
user (any refusal the single settle would give; going to PENDING is not a refusal), none of them is
settled, every one counts as refused and nothing is written. Otherwise every selected claim is
settled in list order as before, and after the claims' own lines one line BATCH_SETTLED
batch=<batch number> count=<claims in the batch> total=<the frozen figures of those SETTLED, added
up> is written.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A bulk settle is now all-or-nothing, and all 4 acceptance tests pass under `bin/e2e`.

**What happens now:**
- **Any refusal stops the whole batch.** If any selected claim would be refused by the single settle, or isn't on the sheet, nothing is settled. Every selected claim counts as refused, no batch number is used, and nothing goes to the audit file. A claim that goes to PENDING still counts as settled, not refused.
- **Otherwise the batch goes through.** Every claim is settled in list order as before. After the claims' own lines (including any ROLLUP/TOTALS lines), one line is written: `BATCH_SETTLED sheet=… by=… batch=<n> count=<claims in the batch> total=<the SETTLED claims' frozen figures added up, two decimals>`. PENDING claims count toward `count` but add nothing to `total`.

**How it's done:**
- **`ClaimBulkService.settle`** now runs the whole bulk settle in one transaction, using the same refusal rules as the single settle. On the first refusal it rolls everything back.
- **No extra work was needed for the audit file.** The audit service already holds lines back until the transaction commits, so a rolled-back batch writes nothing.
- **`ClaimService.settleBatch`** now also takes the user and writes the `BATCH_SETTLED` line.
- **Front end:** no change in behaviour was needed; I only updated the comment on `bulkSettle` in `people.ts`.

Bulk open and bulk reassign are unchanged: each claim still goes through or is refused on its own.

probe.probe_text:
I've read the code and changed nothing. Two things to know first: - **The figures are worked out twice.** The front end computes every number on screen itself (`claimShownCents` and friends in `rates.service.ts`, plus about 20 methods in `people.ts`). The server's `RollupService` computes the same figures again, but only for the audit lines (ROLLUP, TOTALS, SNAPSHOT) and for settling, statements and period closes. The server never sends a live due to the screen. - **There is no import feature.** The nearest things are **paste** (`PasteService`) and **quick-add** (`QuickAddService`). ## 1. Figures and the rules behind them ### Claim row (`claims.ts`) | testid | What it shows / rule | |---|---| | `claim-amount`, `claim-date`, `claim-note`, `claim-ref`, `claim-tags` | Stored values. `Claim.tagsOf`: tags are trimmed, lower-cased, de-duplicated and sorted. A ref must be unique on the sheet, ignoring case (`refuseRefTaken`). | | `claim-number` | Given only at OPEN (`nextNumber`); null while DRAFT. Normally a sheet-wide number (`nextClaimNumber`). Once the sheet's today is on or after `periodNumberingFrom` (`Sheet.numbersByPeriod`), it becomes `-` for the period holding the **due-by**, or `X-` if no period holds it. A VOID claim keeps its number. | | `claim-due` | `claimShownCents` (front end) = `RollupService.shownOf` (server):
1. **frozen** (`isFrozen`/`frozen`): SETTLED, or VOID after being settled, with a `settledDue` → shows `settledDue`.
2. Otherwise, if `stated` and not PENDING → `statedDue`.
3. Otherwise `dueOf` = amount × the rate's `pct` / 100, rounded to 2 places. The rate is the one in force on the **claim's date** for the person's grade on that date (`gradeOn`, `rateOn`/`findInForce`). A rate whose to-date has passed gives none; an earlier rate does not come back.
4. Add the **late charge**, then raise to at least the **floor** in force on the claim's date (`liveDueOf`/`floored`; floor starts at 1.00).
5. A **correction** (negative amount) gets neither late charge nor floor.
6. With no rate the claim shows `n/a`. | | Rounding (`roundingOf`/`roundsHalfUp`) | HALF_UP if the claim is dated before the **policy date in force** (`policyDate`, or the sheet's today when unset). HALF_EVEN on or after it. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects. | | Late charge (`overdueChargeOf`/`lateChargeCents`) | Only on OPEN or PENDING claims that are not deferred. One charge for each full 30 days since `overdueFrom`. Each charge is the late % in force on that 30-day boundary date, applied to the figure plus earlier charges (it compounds), and rounded the claim's way. A 0% boundary adds nothing. Late % starts at 0.00. A statement never binds the late charge. | | `claim-due-by` | `HolidayService.dueBy`: the terms-th business day after `dueFrom` (the claim's date when it was added), skipping weekends and sheet holidays. Terms 0 means the date itself.
Terms are fixed when the claim is added (`termsOf`): the person's own terms, else the grade's terms in force on the claim's date, else the sheet's terms (starting at 14).
Adding a holiday works out the due-by again for every claim that is not SETTLED or VOID and whose due-by is on or after the holiday. A re-date (`redate`) does **not** move the due-by. | | `claim-overdue` | `isOverdue`/`overdue`: OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and `overdueFrom` is before today. `overdueFrom` = due-by plus the grade's grace days in force on the claim's date (`gradeGraceOn`). | | `claim-status` | `ClaimStatus.canBecome`: DRAFT→OPEN/VOID; OPEN→PENDING/SETTLED/VOID; PENDING→OPEN/SETTLED/VOID; SETTLED→VOID; VOID is final. | | `claim-period` | The period whose dates contain the **due-by**, not the claim's date (`periodOn`). | | `claim-deferred`, `claim-deferred-until` | `isDeferredOn`: the claim is OPEN and today is before `deferredUntil`. | | `claim-stated` | Bound by a statement (`bind`/`unbind`). | | `claim-opened-by`, `claim-batch`, `claim-proofs`, `claim-split-from`, `claim-corrects`, `claim-reminded`, `claim-late-entry` | Stored values. `lateEntry` is set when the claim was added with its due-by inside a soft-closed period (`softClosedOn`). | | `claim-log-line` | ` by on due=` (`ClaimService.log`). | ### Which claims count (`countsLive`/`countsAs`, the same rules on server and front end) - The status must be OPEN, PENDING or SETTLED. SETTLED always counts. - An OPEN or PENDING claim is left out when: - it is deferred on today, or - it is unbound (or PENDING) and its date falls in one of the person's holds (`isHeldOn`), or - it is unbound (or PENDING) and the person's `retiredFrom` is on or before today (`isRetiredOn`). - A statement binding (`stated`, and not PENDING) keeps an OPEN claim counting despite a hold or retirement. A deferral still leaves it out. ### Person row (`people.ts`) - **`person-claimed`** (`claimedCentsOf`): the sum of the amounts of counting claims. - **`person-due-total`** (`dueTotalOf`/`dueCentsOf`): the sum of the shown dues of counting claims, capped by the **cap in force on today**. - It shows `n/a` when no counting claim has a figure *and* no rate is in force today for the grade they hold today. - **`person-excess`**: how far the uncapped sum is above the cap (0.00 if it isn't, or if there is no cap). - **`person-settled-total` / `person-open-total`** (`splitOf`): the due-total split into SETTLED claims and OPEN/PENDING claims, before the cap. - **`person-overdue-count` / `person-overdue-total`** (`overdueOf`): counting claims that are overdue. - **`person-aged-0-30` / `-31-60` / `-61`** (`agedOf`): counting OPEN/PENDING claims grouped by days from the claim's date to today. Claims dated after today fall in 0–30. - **`person-period--due-total`** (`personPeriodCents`): - For a closed or soft-closed period, the per-person figure fixed at close (0 for a person added later). - For an open period, the claims with their due-by in it, counted by the status they had at the end of the period's last day (`statusOn`/`statusAt`, read from the status log). A claim that is still open now must also pass the live hold/defer/retire checks. Each is valued as it shows now. - **`person-grade`** (`gradeNow`): the grade in force on today. - **`person-retired`** / **`person-retired-from`**: `retired` is "yes" as soon as any retire date is set, whatever that date is. - **`person-hold`**: "yes" if they have any hold, whatever its dates. - **`person-active`** (`isActive`): they have a counting OPEN/PENDING claim dated in the 30 days up to and including today. - **`person-backing`** (`backings`): for each patron, the frozen figures of that patron's SETTLED claims dated in the 90 days up to and including today, added up. - **`person-statement-count`**, **`person-stated-total`**, **`person-statement-date`**: taken from the person's last statement. ### Sheet totals and summary - **`rollup-claimed-total`**: a plain sum. - **`rollup-due-total`**: `trimmedSum` of the people's due-totals (n/a ones skipped). With three or more figures, the single highest and single lowest are dropped. - **`rollup-overdue-total`**: also trimmed. - **`rollup-overdue-count`**, **`rollup-settled-total`**, **`rollup-open-total`**: plain sums. - **`summary-grade-X-count` / `-due-total` / `-active`**: people who are not retired, grouped by today's grade. - **`summary-period-*`**: the sum of the per-person period figures. - **`tag-*-due-total`**: counting claims carrying the tag; a claim with two tags counts in both. - **`month-*-due-total`**: grouped by the claim's date (yyyy-mm). - **`summary-status-*-count`** and **`summary-void-*-count`**: claim counts by status and by void reason. ### What is frozen, and when - **Settle** fixes `settledDue`: the bound figure (or the rate figure) plus the late charge at that moment, with the floor applied. - It is kept after a void, but a voided claim leaves every total and the void is logged as `reversed=`. - If there was no rate, nothing is fixed and the claim keeps showing `n/a`. - **Approve** (PENDING→SETTLED) fixes the live figure. No statement binds a claim while it is PENDING. - **Resettle** (steward only) fixes the claim again at today's rate, floor and late charge, as if it were an unbound OPEN claim (`openShownOf`). - **Statement** (`StatementService.take`): binds each counting claim to its `figureOf` (the late charge is excluded and keeps following today). Claims that don't count are left unbound. It records a capped due-total. - **As-of** statements rebuild the sheet as it stood then (`SheetAsOf`). - **Cancel last** (steward only) unbinds that statement's claims. An earlier statement's bindings are *not* restored. - **Unbinding**: a split and a reassign both unbind the claim. - **Period close** fixes each person's total for the period and the period's own total. **Reopen** makes them live again. - **Fixed when a claim is added**: `terms` and `dueFrom`. Later changes to terms don't touch existing claims. ### Who may do what - **Roles**: clerk is the default. Steward is given explicitly, or acquired through a delegation while today is inside its date range (`roleOf`). A viewer may change nothing (`ViewerGuard`; bulk actions refuse every claim). - **Permission matrix** (`Action.standing`, which a sheet can override): | Action | Allowed by default | |---|---| | open, settle, void, close | clerk, steward | | reassign, reopen | steward | - **Steward only, hard-coded**: approve, reject, redate, resettle, cancel a statement, archive the sheet, void a SETTLED claim (only up to 7 days after its first SETTLED log date), and delegate (which needs the steward role itself, not one held by delegation). - **No self-approval**: whoever opened or last edited a claim cannot settle or approve it (`isOpenedOrEditedBy`). - **Clerk limit**: a clerk's settle whose due is above the clerk limit in force on today goes to PENDING instead (`overLimit`). A due of n/a passes any limit. - **Proofs**: a settle or approve is refused if the claim has no proofs and its due is above the proof threshold (the grade's own, else the sheet's) in force on the claim's date (`refuseUnproved`). - **Notes**: an open is refused if the note is empty and the due is above the note threshold (`refuseNoteless`). - **Other refusals**: - Only a DRAFT can be edited, and editing it takes a per-user lock that lasts while today stays the same (`isLockedFor`). - A deferred claim cannot be settled. Only an OPEN claim can be deferred, and only to a date after today. - A split only works on an OPEN claim that isn't deferred, and the split amount must be more than 0 and less than the claim's amount. - A claim can be reminded only once per today. - A correction must name a SETTLED claim of the same person. - No claim can be added, edited or re-dated to a date after the person's retirement date (`requireClaimable`). - If a void reason list exists, a void must use one of its reasons. - An archived sheet and the as-of view refuse every change. ### What a date decides The **sheet's today** (`Sheet.today`, never the clock) decides all of the following: - overdue status, the late charge, deferral, the cap, the clerk limit, the grade shown and whether "rated" (for `n/a`); - retirement, the active and backing windows, the 7-day void window, edit locks, and per-period numbering. The **claim's date** decides the rate, grade, floor, late-% table lookups, terms, proof and note thresholds, grace days, rounding against the policy date, holds, and month grouping. The **due-by** decides the period a claim belongs to, closed-period refusals, late-entry, and the number prefix. Changing today also does three things: - writes a SNAPSHOT audit line per person; - releases all edit locks; - auto-closes open periods once their to-date plus the sheet's `graceDays` is before the new today (`closeOverdue`, logged `auto=yes`). ### Holds, closed periods, paste and quick-add - **Hold**: has a from-date (default today) and an optional to-date. It can't be released. Unbound OPEN/PENDING claims dated inside it leave every live total. - **Closed period** (hard close): - Any change to a claim whose due-by is inside it is refused (`refuseClosed`): add, edit, lock, status change, defer, remind, redate, split, proof, reassign, resettle. So is an edit that would move the due-by into it. - The period's figures stay at what was fixed. - **Soft-closed period**: figures are fixed the same way, but claims can still change. New claims due in it are marked late entries. - **Paste**: each `name,amount,date,note[ #ref]` line becomes a DRAFT through the normal add rules. It is all or nothing, and a blank date takes the default. - **Quick-add**: makes a DRAFT dated by the default with an empty note, and creates the person at grade A if they don't exist. Also all or nothing. - **Default date** for a claim left without one: `entryDate` if set, else today. ## 2. How hard it was to follow It's scattered and duplicated, not in one place. The server rules are spread across `RollupService`, `ClaimService`, `PeriodService`, `StatementService`, `HolidayService`, `DatedSettings` and the `Claim`/`Person` entities. The front end then reimplements the whole figure engine separately (`rates.service.ts`, `claims.service.ts`, and about 20 methods in the 1,600-line `people.ts`). Several docs have drifted from the code: the front end's `lateEntry` comment says "date" where the code uses due-by, `claimedCentsOf` says "OPEN and SETTLED" but also counts PENDING, and several refusals say "dated in a closed period" when they check the due-by. A new developer would have to keep the two copies in sync by hand without any single source of truth.
